Subject: MAP: First 50 days & ownership transfer — NovaBio (post-sign)

Hi Asha / Tom — and hi Neha + Karthik,

Thanks again for signing — thrilled to have NovaBio on Redwood. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the "first 50 days" milestones, owners, and evaluation criteria. This is intended to help Sales formally hand the baton to Customer Success and make onboarding deterministic.

High-level ask: can CS own the MAP and confirm owners for each line item by EOB next Thursday (Oct 7)?

Key items in the sheet (attached):
- Week 0: Kickoff meeting, invite list, access provisioning (SLA: infra access verified) — owner: CS
- Week 1–2: Eval plan for integration tests + sample prompts — owner: customer + CS
- Week 3–4: Performance validation (latency, cost), quantization/throughput tuning — owner: Redwood platform engineering + CS contact
- Week 5–7: Final sign-off, rollout plan, success criteria (latency < 250ms p50; accuracy on eval set >= 92%) — owner: Customer stakeholders

Action items for Neha / CS:
1) Confirm CS primary and backup owners for each MAP line.
2) Confirm kickoff meeting date/time options (I put three in the sheet).
3) Review the Eval plan section and flag any gaps.

Attachments: NovaBio_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP), redwood_onboarding_playbook_v2.pdf, signed_master_services_agreement.pdf

I’ve looped in Karthik as CS lead for capacity planning. Neha — can you pick this up as the point for day-to-day coordination?

Thanks!

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — congrats team! Asha / Tom, fantastic to meet you (virtually). I’ll pick up day-to-day ownership and drive the MAP to the agreed milestones. A few quick notes after a first pass through the sheet: 

1) Owners: I propose CS primary = Neha Kapoor, CS backup = Jordan Blake, and Karthik will be escalation lead for capacity/throughput items. I added these to the owner column in the attached map (redlines).

2) Kickoff timing: Of the three options you suggested, Wed Oct 4, 9:00–9:45 PT works best for our team. If that’s good for you, I’ll send the invite and a short agenda (30-min intro + 15-min ops).

3) Eval plan: The test harness looks solid; I recommend adding two additional verification rows: (a) open-ended prompt regression test (50 prompts) and (b) key PII-exfil test cases for your sensitive endpoints. I’ve noted both under Eval -> Additions.

4) Pre-kickoff checklist we’ll complete before the meeting:
- Confirm service account and access to staging VPC (Asha/Tom)
- Share representative prompt set and sample dataset (Asha)
- Confirm expected concurrent session targets (Tom)

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll schedule the Oct 4 kickoff and attach final MAP v1.1 with the owner roster and the two eval additions.
- Karthik / Jordan will prep a 10-minute implementation overview for the meeting (deployment model, monitoring hooks, and rollback plan).

If anything else from Sales we should be aware of (special pricing commitments/credits), please include in the agenda or call it out here.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor | Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 212-555-0188

Thanks Neha — appreciate the quick takeover. A couple of operational notes from infra side before the kickoff: 

- Capacity: For the initial evaluation, recommend we start with a single dedicated slot in ap-specified region (you put "US West" in the MAP). If NovaBio wants to validate higher throughput, we can schedule a dedicated-capacity ramp in Week 3. I added a short note in the MAP under Performance -> Capacity.
- Monitoring: I’ll bring the per-route cost and latency dashboards and a condensed troubleshooting playbook to the kickoff. Jordan, can you prep the runbook link (we should include it in the invite)?
- Integrations: We’ll need the SSO metadata and the kube namespace for staging. Asha, if you can share SSO metadata before Oct 2 that will speed provisioning.

I’ll be on the Oct 4 slot if confirmed.

Hi Neha / team — thank you and congrats to all. Wed Oct 4 at 9:00 PT works for us. I’ve dropped the sample prompt set and a subset of the PII cases into the shared Drive folder (link above). We’ll share SSO metadata no later than EOD Oct 2.

Two asks from NovaBio ahead of kickoff: 
1) Can CS include an example incident response timeline in the runbook? Previously we had a tight window requirement for data-access investigations.
2) For the eval, would Redwood be able to run a small warm traffic test with a controlled set of users in Week 2 (low concurrency, production-like tokens) to validate real-world latency?

We’ll confirm the final invite once Neha sends. Looking forward to the kickoff.
